1. Install Carbon React (v7.x) and Carbon (v10.x) in a fresh React project.
2. Copy the code above into your src/App.js (or TSX) file and ensure you render <App /> into #root.
3. Run the project (e.g. yarn start).
4. Open the browser accessibility inspector or use an assistive-technology simulation.
5. Observe that in the rendered Modal, only the text from the `aria-label` attributes is used for accessibility labeling; the `ariaLabel` props have no effect.
6. In the ComboBox, only the `ariaLabel` (camelCase) property is applied to the underlying input element’s aria-label; the hyphenated `aria-label` prop is ignored.

This reproduces the inconsistency reported: Modal variants require hyphen-case props but most other Carbon components still use camel-case ariaLabel.
1.bug_scenario: In Carbon React v7/v10 the Modal component (and its variants, e.g. ComposedModal/ModalHeader) only accepts the hyphen-cased prop `aria-label`, whereas most other components (e.g. ComboBox, Dropdown, CodeSnippet, OverflowMenu, NumberInput, etc.) still only accept the camel-cased prop `ariaLabel`. This inconsistency means that passing `ariaLabel` to a Modal has no effect (and often TypeScript/PropTypes will warn), and passing `aria-label` to a ComboBox (or Dropdown) also does nothing. Below is a minimal React example demonstrating that: Modal only responds to `aria-label`, and ComboBox only responds to `ariaLabel`.
